record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Let Σ be an alphabet, k ∈ [1, 2], and w ∈ Σ∗ be a k-power-free word. Then in any case, w is a factor of a maximal k-power-free word over Σ.

evidence.quote: Let Σ be an alphabet, k ∈ [1, 2], and w ∈ Σ∗ be a k-power-free word. Then in any case, w is a factor of a maximal k-power-free word over Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite alphabet and let Σ* denote the free monoid of finite words over Σ. For a real number k ≥ 1, a finite word u ∈ Σ* is called a k-power if it can be written as u = v^⌊k⌋ v', where v ∈ Σ* is nonempty, v' is a prefix of v, and |u| / |v| ≥ k. A word w ∈ Σ* is k-power-free if no factor (contiguous subword) of w is a k-power. A k-power-free word w ∈ Σ* is said to be maximal if no word obtained by appending a letter on the left or on the right of w is k-power-free; equivalently, w is maximal if it cannot be extended (on either side) to a strictly longer k-power-free word over Σ.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every finite alphabet Σ, every real number k ∈ [1, 2], and every k-power-free word w ∈ Σ*, there exists a maximal k-power-free word m ∈ Σ* such that w is a factor of m.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is a form of the Restivo–Salemi extendability property for α-power-free languages. It has been established in several cases (notably for binary alphabets and for α ≥ 5 with k ≥ 3 letters in subsequent work), but a full proof for all alphabets and all exponents in [1,2] does not appear in the literature, so the conjecture remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Restivo Salemi property for α-power free languages with α ≥ 5 and k ≥ 3 letters
status_evidence.snippet: Restivo Salemi property has been completely characterized for binary alphabets; partial results exist for ternary alphabets, but a complete characterization remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The Restivo–Salemi extendability property is known in several cases but not fully proved in general.

status_evidence.title: Transition Property for α-Power Free Languages
status_evidence.snippet: Studies extendability/transition properties of α-power free languages, building toward Restivo–Salemi-type conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on extending k-power-free words to maximal ones.
